decision_summary: City council voted unanimously to cancel the Flock contract and remove all 12 cameras after community pushback over data access and privacy. A later council packet shows a $49,000 final-year payout to Flock was made even though the city received no further service, and the contract could otherwise have auto-renewed in May 2027.

decision_summary: The Plymouth City Council voted 6-1 to discontinue the city's Flock Safety surveillance cameras, with the mayor casting the lone dissenting vote. Police leadership had defended the cameras as a safety tool but understood the privacy concerns; residents had raised complaints for months.
